perspective:
Christian’s available information:

- Christian knows he is a police officer and that Jonathan is his close childhood friend, a carpenter with a master’s degree. Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Christian had felt Jonathan was hiding something important, making him anxious and suspicious. He arranged a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop.
- At that meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt Jonathan was hiding something serious. He heard Jonathan ask why he thought that, say Christian could trust him, then admit he had been keeping something from Christian: Jonathan is in trouble and didn’t know how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered help and support, saying he couldn’t just stand by. He heard Jonathan say the situation is complicated, that he didn’t want to drag Christian in, but that he could use support/resources and needed to get out of the mess.
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might involve criminal activity. He felt conflicted and concerned, but decided to investigate discreetly without alarming Jonathan. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. He heard Jonathan say he couldn’t be sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he didn’t do anything illegal himself. Jonathan thanked him and trusted him to handle it carefully.
- Through his investigation, Christian learned/believed Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up. He felt determined and protective. He told Jonathan this, said he didn’t know who yet but had leads, and planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan reacted with surprise and gratitude.
- Christian now believes he has found out who is behind it: someone close to both him and Jonathan, whom they both know and trust. He feels betrayed and resolute. He told Jonathan he would confront the person and make sure they are brought to justice. Jonathan warned him the person is dangerous and said he trusts Christian to do what’s right.
- The provided material does not name the culprit, but Christian believes he knows their identity and knows they are someone close to both of them.
